decision: Did not close the request. Despite an invoice being uploaded (event-023), the record contains no confirmed appointment and no work result: the contractor never selected a slot from the tenant's offered dates (event-014, event-015, event-017) and on 02/09 reported the glass had still not arrived (event-021). The invoice copy (glazing-invoice.pdf, event-023) states no amount, so it cannot be checked against the landlord-approved £180 incl. VAT (event-010) or forwarded for payment. Landlord authority is sound and already on file, so no new approval was sought. I chased the instructed contractor with a 2-working-day reply-by for attendance confirmation, a fitting slot and a priced invoice; asked the tenant to confirm whether anyone attended, whether the unit is still misted and whether damp or mould has appeared (the damp/cold concern was never assessed on site — event-005); updated the landlord that the invoice is not being processed; and placed the case on hold. Not an escalation: the open questions are owned by the contractor and the tenant, and the routine next steps are all reversible.

Our record shows no confirmed attendance for this job. On 02/09 you advised the ordered glass had not arrived and no date could be given, and no slot was ever selected from the tenant's offered dates of 24, 25 or 26 August. An invoice dated 10/09 for "supply and fit 1 pane of glass to the kitchen glazing" has since reached us, and the copy we hold shows no amount.

Before we can report completion or send anything to the landlord, please confirm in writing:
1. Has the glass been fitted? If so, on what date and time did you attend, and who gave access?
2. If it has not been fitted, what is the current delivery position and the first date you can offer? The tenant has asked to be present, so we will need a slot to put to her.

Please reply within 2 working days. If we have no reply by then the case goes to our property manager to review the instruction and the invoice.

Dear Ms Marr,

An update on the kitchen glazing at 8 Brackenmere Walk, and an apology for the time this has taken.

The replacement glass was ordered and the landlord has approved the work, but the contractor has not yet confirmed an attendance date with us, and our file has no record of a visit taking place. We have asked them today to confirm whether anyone has attended and, if not, to give us their first available date, and to reply within 2 working days. We will come back to you with a slot as soon as they do — we will not book anything without agreeing it with you first, and we have kept your note that you wish to be present and that there are pets at the property.

So that the record is accurate, could you let us know:
1. Has anyone attended to fit new glass in the kitchen window? If so, roughly when?
2. Is the kitchen glazing still misted between the panes?
3. Has any damp, black mould or staining appeared around the frame, the reveals or the nearby wall since you reported this in July? A photograph would help.

In the meantime, to limit moisture build-up: wipe standing water from the frame and sill when it gathers, use the extractor fan or open the window briefly when cooking, and keep furniture a little off the external wall. Please tell us straight away if mould appears or spreads — we will treat that as a separate priority rather than waiting for the glazing.

Kind regards,
Northbridge Lettings
